_what: Read from the GitHub REST API (unauthenticated) by spec 041 before the report was written; each field is copied from the response named in responses, whose sha256 is listed. The full responses are kept out of git under specs/000-governance/external-runs/github-20260921T172411Z/ because they carry commit-author addresses.

pulls.title: fix(evals): bind grader results to declared expectations by id
pulls.author: mavericksea-ai
pulls.body:
`parseGrading` (lines 429 to 458 of `scripts/run-evals.js` at be4e44a) validated only that the number of grader results matched the expected count, without binding each result to its declared expectation. A grader response could duplicate one expectation, omit another, include results for undeclared expectations, or supply a fabricated `pass_rate`, and still pass validation.

This change requires every grader result to carry an integer `id` in `1..n` that maps back to the numbered expectations in the prompt, rejects duplicates and out-of-range ids, enforces that every declared expectation is graded exactly once, replaces each result's `text` with the declared expectation so reports carry the canonical wording, and derives `pass_rate` from the validated counters rather than trusting or comparing against the grader's value.

### Prior fixes in the same validator

- #473
- #563

### New tests

1. Reordered but complete results are accepted.
2. Duplicate results (the same expectation graded twice, another omitted) are rejected.
3. Results whose ids are not in the declared set are rejected.
4. A result set that omits a declared expectation is rejected.
5. `summary.pass_rate` is derived from the counters: a grader value of 0.999 with correct counters is accepted and rewritten to the derived value.
6. Paraphrased grader `text` is replaced by the declared expectation.

The new tests fail at be4e44a and pass with this change; the existing tests still pass (22 in total).

### Prompt change

The grader return-schema instruction now includes `"id": integer` and a sentence requiring each id to match the expectation number.

### Changes

- `scripts/run-evals.js`: `parseGrading` signature changed from `(raw, expectedCount)` to `(raw, expectations)`, where `expectations` is the string array; id binding and duplicate and range checks added; result `text` canonicalised from the declared expectation; `pass_rate` derived from the validated counters, with `passed`, `failed` and `total` still required to match exactly; grader prompt updated; call site updated.
- `scripts/run-evals-test.js`: existing `parseGrading` tests updated for the new signature; six new tests added.

pulls.title: fix(hooks): simplify-ignore Stop expands the file on disk instead of restoring a stale backup
pulls.author: mavericksea-ai
pulls.body:
The `Stop` branch of `hooks/simplify-ignore.sh` (line 154 at be4e44a, `cat "$bak" > "$orig"`) restores every cached file from its backup unconditionally. That backup is written once on `PreToolUse Read` (line 202) and refreshed only by the `PostToolUse Edit|Write` branch (line 291), so any change that reaches a protected file through another route between `Read` and `Stop` is silently overwritten at session end: a `Bash` command, a formatter, a generator, an external editor.

Reported in #295 with a live reproduction on Claude Code 2.1.90, the three hooks from `SIMPLIFY-IGNORE.md` passed as `--settings`, and one file holding one protected block plus one unprotected line. The prompt routed the edit through `Bash` and forbade `Edit` and `Write`. With the hooks enabled, `Bash` wrote and read back `const editable = 2;`, the run finished clean, and the file on disk afterwards held `const editable = 1;`. With the hooks disabled, the same task left `const editable = 2;`. No crash, no failed tool call, no symlink, no path alias, no missing dependency: a normal `Stop` event.

### The intent this is measured against

The hook's own header states the contract: "The file on disk ALWAYS has placeholders while the session is active. The real content (with model's changes applied) lives in the backup." The protection is over the *content of the annotated block*, which is hidden from the model behind `BLOCK_<hash>` while the session runs, not over the file as a whole; `SIMPLIFY-IGNORE.md` describes the round trip as "expands placeholders back to real code, saves model's changes". The hook is not documented as reverting a protected file to its pre-session state, and it does not behave that way for `Edit` or `Write`. So the defect is real: `Stop` must not lose a change simply because that change arrived through a tool the hook does not listen to.

Refreshing the backup on every tool that can write does not fix this within the hook's design. `PostToolUse` for `Bash` carries `tool_input.command`, not `tool_input.file_path`, so there is nothing to key the cache on; the hook would have to re-expand and re-filter every cached file after every tool call, and a write from outside Claude Code (a watcher, an editor) still fires no event at all. The state the hook needs is already on disk.

### Fix

At `Stop`, run the same placeholder expansion the `Edit|Write` branch already runs, against the current contents of the file, rather than copying the backup over it. Whatever wrote the file between events wrote it in its filtered form, with the placeholders intact, so expanding it restores the protected blocks *and* keeps the change, from whichever route it came.

The expansion body moved out of the `Edit|Write` branch into an `expand_file src dest fid` function (same code, parameterised) and both branches now call it, so the fuzzy-match and deleted-block warnings apply identically at `Stop`. A small `has_placeholders` helper decides which path `Stop` takes. When no cached `BLOCK_<hash>` is left in the file, the file was rewritten wholesale and the hook can no longer tell where the protected block belongs. In that case it first copies the rewritten file to `.claude/.simplify-ignore-cache/<id>.recovered`, then restores the backup, and warns on stderr with both paths, so neither version is lost; the user merges by hand. That residual case is documented in `SIMPLIFY-IGNORE.md`'s known limitations, next to the existing rename limitation.

With no external write, expansion of the filtered file reproduces the backup exactly, so `Read → Stop` and `Read → Edit → Stop` are unchanged, byte for byte, including files with no trailing newline.

### Tests

Three tests added to `hooks/simplify-ignore-test.sh`, in the harness's existing style, driving the real hook end to end:

- Test 11: `Read`, a model edit plus the `Edit` event, then a write applied straight to the file with no event after it, then `Stop`. Asserts the direct write survives, the stale value is not restored, the earlier `Edit` still survives, the protected block is back, and no placeholder is left behind.
- Test 12: `Read`, a wholesale rewrite that removes every placeholder, then `Stop`. Asserts the backup is restored, `<id>.recovered` holds the rewritten content, and the warning names both paths.
- Test 13: the minimal case, `Read`, a direct write with no event, `Stop`. Asserts the write survives with the block back and no placeholder left.

The full-lifecycle parts are skipped, not failed, where `jq` is absent, matching how test 10 and `session-start-test.sh` handle that machine.

On be4e44a test 11 fails exactly as reported (`Bash write survives Stop: expected 1, actual 0`; `stale backup value not restored: expected 0, actual 1`) and its other assertions pass, which is what makes it a regression test for this bug rather than for the round trip generally.

```
bash hooks/simplify-ignore-test.sh   # 38 passed, 0 failed
```

The rest of the suite is unchanged: `node --test` over the `scripts/` test files is 36 passed, 0 failed; the five validators pass; `node scripts/run-evals.js --min-rank1 95` is 140 checks, rank-1 100%. `hooks/session-start-test.sh` fails on this machine at be4e44a as well, before any change here: `session-start.sh` no longer emits the `priority` field the test asserts. Observed, not changed in this PR.

CI execution for this harness is implemented in #501, which adds a `test-hooks` job running both hook suites, so this PR does not touch the workflow. If #501 does not land, I am happy to add the job here.

### Overlap with open work

- **#501** extends this same harness with three full-lifecycle tests (11 to 13). Test 11 here is #501's test 13 minus its `Edit` event, and I offered it there in #295. #501 changes only the test file and the workflow, not the hook, so the two do not conflict; if it lands first, these tests rebase onto its numbering and helpers.
- **#294** hardens the same hook (symlink guard, atomic rewrite, `perl` removal) but its `Stop` block still copies the backup, and its backup is still written only on `Read` and `Edit|Write`, so it does not reach this case. The two changes touch different lines of the same branch and are straightforward to order either way.

### Changes

- `hooks/simplify-ignore.sh`: expansion extracted into `expand_file`; new `has_placeholders`; the `Stop` branch expands the file on disk, and when no placeholder remains keeps the rewritten file in the cache as `<id>.recovered` before restoring the backup, with a warning naming both paths; header comment updated to describe `Stop` accurately.
- `hooks/SIMPLIFY-IGNORE.md`: `Stop` row of the event table updated; one known limitation added for the wholesale-rewrite fallback, with the recovered path.
- `hooks/simplify-ignore-test.sh`: tests 11 to 13 as above.

pulls.title: fix(evals): remove stale grading and record run identity
pulls.author: mavericksea-ai
pulls.body:
## Summary

- Clear both `.grading.json` and `.grading.raw.txt` at the top of each
  eval iteration, before the executor is invoked, so no stale result file
  can survive an executor or grader crash, and a successful grading
  cannot leave a stale raw file behind.
- Record run identity in each `.grading.json` under a `run` key.
  Shape captured from a local `claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json`
  invocation whose init event reported `claude-opus-4-6[1m]`:
  ```json
  "run": {
    "executor_model": "claude-opus-4-6[1m]",
    "grader_model": "unknown",
    "timestamp": "2026-09-21T12:34:56.789Z"
  }
  ```
  `executor_model` is the `model` field from the stream-json init event
  the executor already emits. `timestamp` is `new Date().toISOString()`
  at write time. The `run` key is only present when the caller provides
  metadata; `persistGradingOutcome` without it writes the grading object
  unchanged.

## Why this isn't covered by #473, #563, or #576

Those PRs hardened `parseGrading` validation (#473 rejected incomplete
summaries, #563 guarded against null expectations, #576 bound results to
declared expectations by id). They all operate at the grading-parsing
layer: they decide whether a grader response is accepted or rejected.

This PR operates at the persistence layer: what happens to the files
**after** that accept/reject decision is made. None of the three PRs
addressed the fact that `RESULTS_DIR` is never cleared and `base` is
derived from the skill and eval id alone, so a previous run's
`.grading.json` survives at exactly the path a collector reads, even
when the current run's grading is rejected. Nor did they record which
model produced the result or when.

## Executor model source

The model is read from the `{"type":"system","subtype":"init","model":"…"}`
event that the executor's `--output-format stream-json` already emits.
The grader model is recorded as `"unknown"` because the grader is a bare
`claude -p` whose output `parseGrading` extracts by regex; switching it
to `stream-json` would break parsing, and adding `--model` is a behaviour
change outside the scope of a recording fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test scripts/run-evals-test.js`: 33 pass (11 new), 0 fail
- [x] `node scripts/run-evals.js`: 140 checks, 0 errors, 100% rank-1
- [x] Each new test fails before its fix and passes after

**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Node 24. CI
(`.github/workflows/test-plugin-install.yml`, job `validate-skills`)
runs `node --test scripts/run-evals-test.js` and
`node scripts/run-evals.js --min-rank1 95`, so both the unit tests and
the deterministic eval gate execute on every push and pull request.

release.name: Agent Skills 0.6.10
release.body:
Agent Skills 0.6.10 is a reliability and platform release. It changes one default behavior worth reading first, fixes the Windows SessionStart failures, closes a data-loss bug in the simplify-ignore hook, tightens the eval and validator tooling, and lands a wave of cross-host portability docs.

## Behavior change (read this first)

- **The plugin no longer auto-injects the `using-agent-skills` meta-skill on SessionStart** (#574, @santhiprakash, fixes #569). Claude Code and Codex already discover and activate skills from their descriptions, so the old hook was stacking a second router on top of the native one, the pattern our own `getting-started.md` warns against, and it cost roughly 3.5k tokens per session for no gain on those hosts. The standalone `hooks/session-start.sh` stays in the repo as an opt-in helper for hosts without native skill routing. If you were relying on the meta-skill being force-loaded every session, wire that script into a `SessionStart` hook yourself.

## Reliability and platform

- **Windows SessionStart failures fixed** (#488, #475). They were caused by the hook above being run through PowerShell; removing the plugin-registered hook removes the failure entirely.
- **simplify-ignore no longer loses work on Stop** (#578, @mavericksea-ai). It now expands the current file contents instead of blindly restoring the backup, with a `.recovered` fallback for wholesale rewrites.
- **SessionStart payload test fixed and wired into CI** (#510, @santhiprakash). It now asserts the correct `hookSpecificOutput` envelope, replacing an assertion that was stale on main, and runs on every PR.

## Evals and validators

- **skill-lint handles every CommonMark fence form** (#568, @ayobamiseun, fixes #437). A real line-by-line scanner replaces the single regex, so tilde fences, indented fences, and longer closers are all recognized; its test is now wired into CI.
- **The eval grader is stricter** (#576, @mavericksea-ai). Each grader result is bound to a declared expectation by id, the canonical expectation text overrides the grader's paraphrase, and pass_rate is recomputed rather than trusted. Paired with rejecting null grader expectations without crashing (#563, @RogueTex).
- **Reference-link check exempts fenced examples** (#517, @abhisheksharma2411) so an example link inside a code block is no longer treated as a link to resolve, while a real broken link outside a fence still fails.
- **Reference-link assertion is portable on Windows** (#573, @dajiaohuang).
- **Routing description gaps closed and the rank-1 floor raised to 95** (#434, @ayobamiseun).

## Docs and portability

- **Don't stack a second router on native skill hosts** (#557, @kaluli123123), the guidance the behavior change above now matches.
- **Authoring rule against model-specific workarounds** (#545, @ayobamiseun, from #534): write the procedure, not the workaround around one model's failure.
- Cross-host portability and clarity: map the shared core to native adapters (#560), define restartable task boundaries (#559), clarify external artifact ownership (#554), setup for existing projects (#553), the stable browser skill name (#552), and link runnable workflow tutorials (#556), all @kaluli123123. README skill count corrected to 25 (#570, @abhisheksharma2411).
- **Context Budget Management** added to context-engineering (#447, @HMAKT99), plus SLOs and error budgets and runbook guidance across observability and shipping (#415, #422, @HMAKT99).
- Incomplete-plan guard mirrored across tools (#531, @ayobamiseun, from #518).

## Thanks

Thanks to everyone who contributed and reviewed this release: @santhiprakash, @mavericksea-ai, @ayobamiseun, @kaluli123123, @abhisheksharma2411, @HMAKT99, @dajiaohuang, @RogueTex, @nucliweb, and @federicobartoli.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/compare/0.6.9...0.6.10
